examples.turoyo: I+klabṯo hiwoli b̚mašruqo. Noše layto dmoǧaq qarʕi’.
examples.translation: The bitch, I gave her for a flute. There isn’t anybody who can smash my head’. (NE Old Lady and a Bird: 49). ʕabdul‿Masīḥ, the son of Nisane, also knows this verb.
examples.raw:
I+klabṯo hiwoli b̚mašruqo. Noše layto dmoǧaq qarʕi’.
The bitch, I gave her for a flute. There isn’t anybody who can smash my head’. (NE Old Lady and a Bird: 49). ʕabdul‿Masīḥ, the son of Nisane, also knows this verb.
Li+ʕáraba mǧəqla qarʕe ‘The car smashed his head’ (p.c. Faulus from Bequsyone, 1976)

notes: mǧəqle/moǧaq SL 23-8-2025: the verb looks like an adaptation of pčq, a borrowing from Kurmanji, keeping the same meaning. It is used in Bequsyone, along with pčəqle and mparčaqle
